description: Git bulk ops — investigation + workflow combos in one call

git-status.description: Branch, commits + base divergence, changes, stashes, open MR/PR with diff size. A two-sided `ahead N, behind M` gains a `Diverged:` line saying which kind it is — REBASED (every remote commit is patch-equivalent to one you already have; nothing lost, force-with-lease) vs a genuine divergence naming how many remote commits are not in your history, or a stated UNKNOWN when that check did not answer. `:full` (alias `:porcelain`) uncaps every file/branch/stash list — full untruncated view for driving precise staging. `:brief` drops the local-branch inventory and the commit log so the working tree and the MR/PR block sit at the top; a section that could not be read is never dropped. An unrecognised mode is reported, not ignored

git-investigate.description: File history: commits, uncommitted, blame hotspots

git-diff.description: Review-aware diff: classified files + +/-, red-flag scan of added lines (debug code/conflict markers w/ file:line), forbidden-path guard, missing-test pairing, next hints. Add trailing :full (any mode) to append the raw +/- hunks under ## Patch. Policy via .supertool.json ops.git-diff.{red_flags_extra,forbidden_paths,test_pairing,hints}

git-blame.description: Git blame N lines around LINE

git-checkout.description: Switch to REF — branch, tracking, dirty, last commits

git-diverge.description: Branch vs base — ahead/behind, commits, files, +/- totals

git-merge.description: Merge REF — on conflict: UU files, markers, ours/theirs SHAs

git-conflicts.description: List UU files + every conflict block + abort hint

git-resolve.description: Pick ours/theirs/both(union) for PATH (single, comma-separated list, or 'all') + stage + continue cmd. Optional 1-indexed BLOCKS selector (single file) resolves only those conflict blocks (as git-conflicts numbers them); a partial resolve keeps the other blocks' markers and stays unstaged ('N of M blocks resolved'). 'both' is REFUSED per file on source extensions (.py/.js/.php/.sh/... — a union concatenates two versions of code, the result parses, the block runs twice): the file is left conflicted, the tally reads 'Refused: N', and a mixed set still resolves its non-source files. Ways through: append 'force' (the tally then discloses how many source files were unioned), or declare the path merge=union in .gitattributes, which is honoured without a flag. 'both' is ALSO refused on a Markdown file when the union would DUPLICATE A HEADING — the same heading line on both sides of one hunk, which a line-level union emits twice and which reparents every line between the two copies under the first (a Keep a Changelog release heading turns unreleased entries into shipped ones). The refusal names the heading; only 'force' gets through, merge=union does not, and an ordinary changelog conflict (two bullets under a shared heading) is untouched. WITHOUT BLOCKS, ours/theirs is `git checkout --SIDE` — a WHOLE-FILE op: it can silently rewrite content outside any conflict block that diverged between the sides (auto-merged cleanly, no markers). The receipt discloses this on a second line: any line outside every block, by range ('1 conflict block(s), 2 hunk(s) changed — 1 outside any conflict (lines 434-436)') — the 'outside' clause is the signal, not the raw hunk-vs-block count. Prints 'not available' rather than falling silent if the pre/post snapshot couldn't be read; omitted only for 'both' (in-place rewrite, cannot touch anything outside a block)
git-resolve.syntax: git-resolve:::SIDE:::PATH[,PATH...][:::BLOCKS][:::force]  (SIDE: ours|theirs|both; BLOCKS: e.g. 1,3 — single file only; force: union source files anyway)

git-worktrees.description: Is an agent working in this worktree? Answers OWNERSHIP for every worktree (or one PATH): branch, path, occupancy, merge state, uncommitted work and tracker state. INSPECTION ONLY: nothing is removed, pruned, unlocked or written, and no removal command is ever printed. Every column carries a third state naming what could not be looked at, and none of them may collapse into its reassuring neighbour. OCCUPANCY: `occupied`, `idle`, `cannot tell` — the majority answer is `cannot tell` and it is NOT `idle`; `idle` is earned only when every probe answered, the tree stat'd and quiet AND the process table read and holding nobody (locks, an in-progress rebase/merge/cherry-pick, `git worktree lock`, a write newer than SUPERTOOL_WORKTREE_ACTIVE_WINDOW=900s, a process cwd'd inside the tree — /proc on Linux, `lsof -d cwd` elsewhere, Windows declines by name; `idle` also needs quiet for SUPERTOOL_WORKTREE_IDLE_QUIET=3600s). MERGE: `merged` (an ancestor of the base whose reflog shows the ref moved, OR a merged PR with this head — the evidence line says which), `not merged`, `no commits yet`, `merge unknown` with its reason. Ancestry is a POSITIVE ONLY, never a `no`: a squash leaves none, and a branch that never committed satisfies it by holding nothing. TRACKER: `PR #N` with the check tally, `no open PR`, `no remote ref`, `PR unknown` — never rendered as `no open PR`. On by default; `nopr` or SUPERTOOL_WORKTREE_PR=0 drops it and the op is then fully offline. DIRTY, on every row, branch or not: `clean`, `dirty: N`, `dirty unknown` — a scan that failed or timed out is `dirty unknown`, never `clean`. Unknown-merge, dirty and dirty-unknown counts ride the `[result]` line. With a PATH the SCRIPT exits 0 only for `idle` AND clean (1 occupied, 2 cannot tell or the op could not answer at all — a PATH matching more than one worktree included, 3 idle but holding uncommitted work); all four are declared `exitStatus` values, so they are this op's answer and never a verdict on it, and only `0` is `clean`. Through supertool the integer collapses to 0 or 1 — all of 1/2/3 mean do-not-reap; branch on the integer by running `presets/git/worktrees.py` directly. Do not read the exit code as an authorization: read the `[result]` tally. The tracker column stays out of the integer, the dirty column is in it. Full contract and the incident behind each column: docs/presets/git.md.

git-commit.description: Commit MESSAGE (stages PATHS) — Repo (which repository this wrote to, stamped before staging so it survives a hook rejection), HEAD before/after, hook errors surfaced. COMMITS ONLY THE PATHS YOU NAME (#1228): it used to run `git add <paths>` then a pathspec-less `git commit`, so anything another process had staged rode in — on 2026-08-09 that swept up a staged revert and silently un-did 139 lines of a production fix, while the worktree still held the correct file and the tests still passed against the worktree. Foreign staged changes now stay staged, and the receipt names them (`N path(s) were already staged and are NOT in this commit`) read from the index AFTER the commit rather than from the working tree, which is why the original receipt named the very two files it had just committed. Omitting PATHS still commits the index exactly as it stands — the deliberate spelling for `commit what I staged by hand`. During a merge or cherry-pick the pathspec stands down, because git refuses a partial commit there outright. A MESSAGE containing ':' — every Conventional Commits subject — MUST use the triple-colon form or the @payload route: the single-colon CLI splits on every ':' and would hand the tail to `git add` as a pathspec. PATHS are separated by ':::' — not by commas, not by spaces — and both routes stage, the payload one via a `paths` list. MESSAGE=amend (or --amend) is REFUSED: there is no amend route, so committing it made a commit subject-lined 'amend'; use `git commit --amend` directly, or SUPERTOOL_ALLOW_LITERAL_AMEND=1 for the literal subject. A PATH that is neither path-shaped (no whitespace/quotes) nor known to git (on disk, tracked, or an already-staged deletion) is taken as that split and REFUSED before anything is staged, naming both working routes; it is never folded back into the message, because guessing wrong that way commits the already-staged fileset under a mangled subject. A path-shaped PATH git does not know still gets git's own pathspec error. MESSAGE=--no-edit reuses MERGE_MSG/CHERRY_PICK msg (merge or cherry-pick must be in progress). Auto-appends a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer when absent; identity via .supertool.json ops.git-commit.coauthor (default 'Max <noreply>'; set '' / 'none' to disable). Multi-line body: use the @file route — git-commit:@- (stdin) or git-commit:@msg.toml — with a `message` field (subject + blank line + body) and optional `paths` list; the trailer is still appended. Omitting PATHS is refused with the CAUSE, not the symptom (#1155): `no PATHS were given — git-commit never stages for you, so nothing staged`, on the FIRST line, because the `--- op ---` header has already replayed the whole message above it. The other three openings say `the N path(s) you named held no changes`, `the working tree is clean`, or that `git status` did not answer — four situations, four sentences, never one wording for all of them. PATHS=--all is the explicit opt-in (#1137) that accepts the dirty list the refusal just counted (modified tracked + untracked, ignored excluded) instead of sending you to a raw `git status --porcelain` to rebuild it; the receipt then names EVERY path uncapped, since under --all the caller never typed the list. It is refused beside a named path, refused when git knows a file literally called `--all` (use `./--all`), and refused when `git status` did not answer — never resolved into a commit. `paths = ["--all"]` spells the same thing on the @payload route.

git-push.description: Push current branch (sets upstream if missing). ALWAYS ends on a one-line `[result]` verdict — PUSHED / NOT PUSHED (already up to date | REJECTED | REBASE PAUSED | UNVERIFIED | no push attempted) with branch → remote/ref @ sha — so the answer survives `| tail -3`. The post-push sha is read back off the real remote via ls-remote and labelled verified/unverified; a sha that was not read is never printed as if it were. Receipt: Repo (which LOCAL repository these commits came from), remote before/after, ahead/behind, MR/PR + pipeline, mergeability, behind-target, uncommitted-leftover COUNT (list: git-status:full), watch cmd. Non-ff auto-rebases (conflict → paused + git-conflicts). Hook amend+push reported as PUSHED. A push that outlasts its budget is verified against the remote ref before any verdict — landed = PUSHED. A fetch/rebase on the non-fast-forward recovery path that outlasts its own budget reports the WORKTREE state — rebase in progress (with continue/abort), not started, or explicitly unknown — instead of a traceback. The stale-base check follows the branch's real upstream remote (not a hardcoded origin) and says `skipped` when the target ref does not resolve, so silence means only `checked, base is fresh`. On a branch with NO upstream the push remote is RESOLVED, not assumed: branch.<name>.pushRemote, remote.pushDefault, branch.<name>.remote (git's own order), then `origin` if it exists, then the only remote if there is exactly one — so `git clone -o gitlab` and fork/upstream layouts work. Two or more remotes with none named origin and nothing configured is REFUSED (exit 1, nothing pushed) naming the candidates, because creating a branch on a guessed remote is not recoverable by an error message. A resolved remote or ref that begins with `-` is REFUSED by name before any argv is built: those keys are read verbatim (git accepts a URL in them) and `git push -u --receive-pack=<cmd> HEAD` runs <cmd> — git eats the option and spawns receive-pack for the local path `HEAD` before failing to find a repository there (observed, git 2.46.2; #818, #1617). Flags: :force-with-lease, :no-verify, :budget=SECONDS (how long this op may spend PUSHING, in place of the 300s default; a DEADLINE for the whole pushing phase, not a per-call timeout — the non-fast-forward recovery's fetch, rebase and re-push all draw from what is left of it, and a phase with nothing left is declined as `NOT PUSHED - BUDGET SPENT` rather than launched on an expired clock (#1615) — the flag to reach for when a pre-push hook runs a test suite, which is where :no-verify is least appropriate; capped at 1800s, and an unreadable, non-positive, contradicted or over-cap value is REFUSED before anything is pushed rather than clamped; the DEFAULT itself is settable per repository as ops.git-push.budget in .supertool.json — precedence :budget > ops.git-push.budget > 300 — validated against ops.git-push.timeout FROM THE SAME MERGED ENTRY and refused naming both numbers, before anything is pushed, when it is not strictly under it (#1631)), :watch (spawns a background pipeline poller; falls back to the running interpreter + supertool.py where the ./supertool wrapper is absent, e.g. a git worktree, and names the reason if it cannot start). An UNKNOWN flag is REFUSED before anything is pushed (exit 2) — never silently dropped. An upstream that resolves to a DIFFERENT branch — the default outcome of `git worktree add -b <new> <base>`, so every st-wt/NNN branch starts here — is still refused rather than guessed through, but both ways out are now flags on this op instead of raw `git push` lines the caller's own hook may forbid: `:set-upstream` pushes the branch under its own name and retargets tracking to <remote>/<branch> (the usual first push), `:to-upstream` pushes onto the tracked ref on purpose with an explicit refspec. Asking for both is REFUSED (exit 2) naming the two targets — they are different refs and precedence would be the guess the refusal exists to prevent.
